question.text:
The heats of neutralisation of $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{COOH}$, $\mathrm{HCOOH}, \mathrm{HCN}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{~S}$ are -13.2,-13.4,-2.9

and $-3.8 \mathrm{kCal}$ per equivalent respectively. Arrange the acids in increasing order of acidic strength.

solution.text:
The greater the (negative value) of heat of neutralisation, the more is the strength of the acid. Hence,

$$

\mathrm{HCOOH}>\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{COOH}>\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{~S}>\mathrm{HCN}

$$
